name: BuiltWorlds: AI in Construction Research, News and Company Profiles
title: BuiltWorlds: AI in Construction Research, News and Company Profiles
answer: BuiltWorlds publishes AI-focused construction technology research, news, reports and company profiles. Its AI/ML Preparedness Research Track uses working group sessions and benchmarking to examine adoption trends, use cases, investment priorities and challenges. The most useful single item for a construction reader is the 2025 AI: Use Cases & Operational Impact Tech Specialty Report, which describes AI applied across large language models, agentic AI, computer vision and predictive analytics in project management, preconstruction, field management, robotics and building technology.

sections.body: BuiltWorlds publishes a website that combines news, research track pages, report descriptions, videos and company profiles. Its AI/ML Preparedness Research Track is aimed at organizations navigating AI and machine learning in the built environment, using working group sessions and industry benchmarking. The site describes three 2025 tech specialty reports on AI strategy, investment and priorities, AI use cases and operational impact, and AI challenges, perceptions and future outlook. It also publishes a 2026 list of 40 AI-driven AEC solutions, a Q3 2024 deal activity article, profiles such as Zesty.ai and Concrete-AI, and event sessions scheduled from February 2026 to September 2027.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: BuiltWorlds says its AI/ML Preparedness Research Track equips organizations with insights and strategies for AI and machine learning in the built environment. It uses dynamic working group sessions and in-depth industry benchmarking analyses. Participants gain understanding of adoption trends, emerging use cases and future opportunities, identify key datasets and methods, understand AI's measurable value, assess major sector technology companies, explore academia, industry and government collaboration, and identify new opportunities. Members get exclusive access to track-specific reports, including the 2025 AI: Strategy, Investment, & Priorities report, the 2025 AI: Use Cases & Operational Impact report, and the 2025 AI: Challenges, Perceptions, & Future Outlook report. Working group sessions are exclusive, closed-door gatherings for members, facilitated by BuiltWorlds and led by expert speakers, held virtually and at BuiltWorlds events. The use cases report says AI is applied across large language models, agentic AI, computer vision and predictive analytics with machine learning. It focuses on data-intensive processes in project management and preconstruction, including scheduling, cost estimation and risk assessment, and on field management, equipment and robotics software and building technology, where AI supports safety monitoring, autonomous operations and smart building management. The strategy report says approaches vary and there is no single path, with adoption ranging from proprietary in-house solutions to AI features in existing software and AI-native tools. The challenges report describes cautious optimism. A news article lists 40 AI-driven AEC solutions to watch in 2026, including Articulate, Beam AI, Boon, Document Crunch, Drawer AI, Firmus, LeanCon, Mercator and Togal AI.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source gives several figures. It says the 2026 list highlights 40 AI solutions. It reports that BuiltWorlds' Deal Dashboard tracked investments in 12 unique building tech companies incorporating AI/ML in Q3 2024, totaling approximately $213 million, and approximately $220 million across 11 construction tech solutions. Among six AI-powered infrastructure companies, deal size data was available for four, amounting to a combined $29 million. It says Zesty.ai leverages more than 115 billion data points on 140 million US homes. It states an estimated $6.7 trillion in investment is needed to meet global data center demand by 2030. It also lists event dates from February 17, 2026 to September 2027.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in construction would use BuiltWorlds to track how the sector is adopting AI, where investment is going, which use cases are emerging, and what obstacles remain. The AI/ML Preparedness Research Track and its 2025 reports frame adoption across large language models, agentic AI, computer vision and predictive analytics, with attention to project management, preconstruction, field management, robotics and building technology. The 40-solution list and company profiles provide a vendor and startup view, while the deal article gives quarterly investment context. The working group sessions and conference dates offer a way to follow practitioner discussion, though much of the detailed material is reserved for members.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Construction

sections.body: The pages describe reports and sessions rather than reproducing the full reports, and some content is exclusive to AI/ML Research Track members. The deal data is from Q3 2024, while the solution list is a 2026 watch list rather than an evaluation. Company profiles are brief. The video page includes promotion for an upcoming conference. The source is commercial, with membership, events and limited spots at working group sessions, so it is best used as a guide to BuiltWorlds' research and network rather than as a complete independent study.
